aggregation of the photosensitizer molecules in QD/PS systems can lead to a decrease in the efficiency of energy transfer between the components of the system, which is undesirable in photodynamic therapy.

the formation of nonluminscent aggregates of aluminium sulphonated phthalocynaine in complexes with Cdse/Zns quantum dots causes a significant decrease in the intracomplex transfer efficiency of the absorbed energy to quantum dots with increasing phthalocyaine concentration.

the aggregation of aluminum sulfonated phalocyanine in the complexes with CdSe-ZnS quantum dots leads to the formation of non-luminescent aggregates and a decrease in the energy transfer efficiency between the phthalocyanines and quantum dots.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of new phthalocyanines with a high potential in photodynamic therapy.
the development of new approaches to the design of nanomaterials with desired properties for various applications.

the study of the influence of phthalocyaine aggregation on the photophysical and photochemical properties of complexes of aluminium sulfonate phthalocyanines with quantum dots of cadmium selenide/zinc sulfide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the nonluminescent phthalocyanines aggregates is not a necessary and sufficient condition for the inhibition of intracomplex energy transfers.

the formation of nonluminscent aggregates of aluminium sulphate phthalocyanines in complexes with CdS/ZnS quantum dot decreases the efficiency of intracomplex energy trasnfer with an increase of phthalocynine concentration.

the aggregation of aluminium sulfonatophthalocyanine (ASPC) in complexes with CdS/ZnS quantum dot (QD) is responsible for the decrease in the intracomplex transfer efficiency with an increase in the phthalocyanines concentration.

the aggregation of the photosensitizing molecule in the complex with the quantum dot is the reason for the decrease of intracomplex energy efficiency.
the aggregation of molecules in QD complexes can lead to a decrease of the photophysical properties, which is undesirable for photodynamic therapy.

the aggregation of phthalocynine molecules in the complex with CdSe/ZnzS quantum dots leads to the formation of non-luminescent aggregates, the efficiency of the energy transfer in the complexes decreases with an increase in the phthalocyanin concentration, which can be explained by the developed physical model.

the photophysical properties and the efficiency of intracomplex energy transfers in the complexes can be controlled by varying the phthalocyanines concentration.
